messages:
tyler: FYI, we just saw cross-tenant egress coming out of rack-12-az3 — looks like VLAN leakage into the public subnet. Customer A + B reported traffic spikes and one hit 5xx from downstream (NAT saturation). Anyone available to triage?

neha: on it. Which nodes and do we have a pcap?

tyler: uploaded pcap to gs://redwood-debug/6151230000/rack12.pcap. affected nodes: gpu-node-az3-17..20. tcpdump shows flows to 18.206.12.0/24 that should have been isolated per VLAN policy.

sam: ugh — we rolled the TOR trunk changes last night. Possible misapplied VLAN map on tor-3. I can pull the running config and diff.

eva: if TOR is the culprit, let's avoid infra-wide pushes. Suggest temporary host-side tenant shielding (iptables + tc) so blast radius is limited while we fix the TOR.

neha: +1. Sam, can you validate TOR config? Tyler, can you also run a quick arp/mac dump from the 4 nodes?

tyler: running: `arp -an | grep tor-3` shows a couple of unexpected MACs on br0. pcap shows eth.dst not matching expected tenant MACs.

sam: looking at tor-3 now. There's a stale trunk rule for VLAN 310 that maps to native VLAN on port 42. didnt get picked up in review. I'll prepare rollback.

eva: Shielding snippet (host-side) I use for emergencies, can be applied on the node quickly:

```bash
# shield tenant X on host
ip netns add shield-X || true
ip link add v-shield type veth peer name v-host || true
ip link set v-shield netns shield-X
ip netns exec shield-X ip link set v-shield up
ip netns exec shield-X ip addr add 10.10.X.1/32 dev v-shield
# limit egress to reduce NAT blast
tc qdisc add dev v-host root tbf rate 100mbit burst 32k latency 50ms || true
# drop packets not matching tenant MAC (example)
iptables -I OUTPUT -m mac ! --mac-source AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF -j DROP || true
```

neha: thanks — that should buy us time. Note: host shielding will break multi-homed containers if misapplied, so we should be surgical (gpu-node-17..20 only).

sam: alternative is routing fallback: add route for tenant subnet -> dedicated-pool within same AZ or another AZ. Pros: less host fiddling. Cons: increases latency and egress cost. Product needs to sign off for user-visible failover.

tyler: routing fallback also changes path; some customers are sensitive to SLOs. We should prefer host shielding + TOR fix if possible.

neha: agreed. Plan proposal: 1) Apply host iptables shielding on gpu-node-17..20 2) sam will rollback the tor-3 trunk rule and redeploy 3) validate with tcpdump for 5m 4) if tor fix delayed >15m, consider migrating affected tenant to dedicated pool in same AZ (cost delta ~ $0.27/hr per GPU slot) 5) postmortem.

infra-bot: deploybot started run 6151230000 on tor-3 config-check

sam: I'm pulling the diff now, will open PR for rollback. Putting @ops-oncall on watch for NAT gateway errors.

eva: also proposing we deploy a tiny eBPF flow-checker to nodes to detect MAC-to-VLAN mismatches and surface an alert (rate threshold: >5 mismatches/min). I can prototype.

neha: please add runbook step for "vlan leakage" with the host-shielding commands and how to revert. I'll own the postmortem.

tyler: alert fired at 13:06 PDT, customer spike lasted ~7m. NAT returned 502s and timeouts. Account team notified.

sam: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/tor-config/pull/329 . Rolling in 2m with 15m rollback window.

infra-bot: deploybot succeeded on tor-3 in 38s.

tyler: re-ran tcpdump on gpu-node-17..20 after deploy — pcap shows no cross-tenant flows now. MACs line up with tenant mappings.

eva: will push eBPF probe to prod in ~90m. That probe will generate a perf event + slack alert for any MAC mismatch rate >5/min.

neha: follow-ups: - add quick shield script to runbook - cost estimate for tenant migration + who to call for approval - monitor NAT gateway metrics for 24h - schedule postmortem for tomorrow 09:30 PT

tyler: thanks everyone. Closing once postmortem doc is up. :thumbsup:
